MEMORANDUM FOR RECORD

SUBJECT: LD 1430, An Act to Promote the Welfare of Disabled Veterans Through the Transfer of
Moose Permits

Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on Inland Fisheries and Wildlife,
1. Thank you for allowing me to bring forth my bill, An Act to Promote the Welfare of Disabled
Veterans Through the Transfer of Moose Permits.
2. For a disabled veteran, the opportunity to participate in outdoor activities can be a very therapeutic experience. The ability to connect with other veterans in sportsman's activities has proven itself to offer
relief for numerous veterans who suffer from the post traumatic stress syndrome caused by the unique
stresses of combat. Additionally it allows warriors a normalizing experience surrounded by their peers.
We know this from the abundant ntunber of successful Veteran Service Organizations that utilize outdoors experiences in Maine, including hunting. My wife and I, both veterans, have personally
benefited from participating in bird hunts organized by a Veterans Service Organizations.
3. As members of this committee, I am sure you are aware that after successfully having drawn a
moose tag in the State of Maine one must wait for three years before being eligible to apply for another
permit or to start collecting points.
4. This bill simply allows for the transfer of a moose tag by a Registered Maine Guide, Veteran Service Organization, or an employee or volunteer of such an organization, to a disabled veteran and

10044512:
Joel Vail Nanoq Guide Services and Survival Training LD 1430
There is a public hearing for bill, LD 1430 An Act to Promote the Welfare of Disabled Veterans Through the Transfer of Moose Permits, this coming Wednesday, the 16th, at 10:00.
This bill would allow Registered Guides, Veteran Service Organizations (VSOs) and employees and volunteers of VSOs to transfer their moose permits to disabled veterans and then allow them to immediately start collecting points and apply for a new permit the following year, eliminating the normal waiting period.
I am a disabled veteran, registered main guide, and founder director of a veteran oriented nonprofit vso. Nanoq Guide Services and Survival Training.
I support this bill because I think that many people who receive the coveted Moose tag are not able to attend for various reasons and will feel more willing to transfer to those organizations or individuals who fit the criteria under this bill. I have seen Hunters choose not to use their tag even though they couldn't hunt because they waited so long to get one. Others were frustrated because they had limited time to do a transfer when they didn't know any veterans that met the criteria personally. Due to the overwhelming volume of other events many of the organizations that would try to help could not respond fast enough either. This solves many problems to eliminate those type of issues and allow groups who are really invested in helping disabled veterans utilize this opportunity better. I think the fact that a vso is able to collect donated tags is logistical bonus to helping those in need within our veteran community. I hope that we will see a simple form online that can be filled out electronically to handle the transfers without phone calls or emails necessary with the state. I know how busy state employees are and that things can be lost in communication so I think that making this a seamless process will be very beneficial. Thank you for taking the time to read this.

TESTIMONY OF THE DEPARTMENT OF INLAND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE
BEFORE THE JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON INLAND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE
NEITHER FOR NOR AGAINST L.D. 1430
"An Act to Promote the Welfare of Disabled Veterans Through the Transfer of
Moose Permits"
Sponsored by: Representative PERKINS of Dover-Foxcroft. (BY REQUEST)
Cosponsored by Senator STEWART of Aroostook and Representatives: CHAPMAN of
Auburn, DILL of Old Town, FREDETTE of Newport, MCINTYRE of Lowell, SOBOLESKI of Phillips, THORNE of Carmel, WHITE of Guilford, WHITE of
Ellsworth
DATE OF HEARING: Wednesday, April 16, 2025
Good morning Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts and members of the Inland
Fisheries and Wildlife Committee. I am Timothy Peabody, Deputy Commissioner of the
Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife, speaking on behalf of the Department, neither for nor against to L.D. 1430.
This bill amends the laws governing moose permit transfers to disabled veterans for certain organizations or individuals if they meet certain eligibility requirements: l. Nonprofit veteran aid organizations based in this State that promote the mental and emotional welfare of veterans in this State by providing outdoor opportunities; 2. The employees and volunteers of nonprofit veteran aid organizations based in this State that promote the mental and emotional welfare of veterans in this State by providing outdoor opportunities; and 3. Registered Maine guides who are residents of this State.
The bill allows for eligible organizations or individuals who obtain a moose permit in the
lottery to transfer the permit to a disabled veteran, the eligible organization or individual
can apply for a moose permit again the following year and may also start accumulating
points for the public chance drawing for a moose permit the following year.
The Department supports efforts to provide disabled veterans more opportunities to hunt and fish in Maine. Currently law and rule, allows several opportunities for disabled veterans to obtain a moose permits. Each year the Department supports a depredation hunt in Aroostook County. Thirty permits are provided for disabled veterans to take moose that are causing damage to broccoli fields in eastern Aroostook County. They have an additional opportunity in current law where any person who receives a moose permit

can transfer that permit to a disabled veteran. The Department works with the Department of Veteran's Affairs in both of these situations to facilitate distributing these permits for
qualified veterans.
In 2024, we had 39 moose permits donated to disabled veterans from over 4,000 moose
permits drawn in the regular moose lottery which included the 4A Adaptive Hunt.
MDIFW successfully matched the 34 permits with disabled veterans. Five Adaptive Hunt
permits were not matched with a disabled veteran. As previously mentioned MDIFW
works closely with the Bureau of Veteran's Affairs to find qualified veteran hunters. We
are also asked by individual permit winners to transfer their permit to a qualified disabled
veteran that they know personally.
Section 2 and 3 of the bill allows certain organizations and employees of these organizations to re-enter the year after winning a permit provides them with a chance to
participate in two hunts in two consecutive years. This added opportunity for those who transfer their permits has a negative impact on the other general applicants who apply but
don't receive a permit. This system is designed to enhance the likelihood of success for
those who have not won recently, while still enabling the permit holder to accumulate
bonus points for future applications. This approach ensures that they can leverage these
points when they are eligible to enter the lottery again, allowing for a balance between
rewarding past winners and giving others a fair chance.
Section 4 of the bill pertains to resident registered Maine guides. The proposed language is very challenging to follow, but it appears to allow a guide to transfer a permit to a disabled veteran without renumeration and retain their (the guides) ability to apply for a
permit again the following year.
In closing if the Committee chooses to move the bill forward consideration needs to be made to the administrative implementation of this opportunity.
I would be glad to answer any questions at this time or during the work session.
